stories.title: Lise Klaveness: ‘Certainly there are people that can challenge Infantino’
summary: Norwegian federation president distances self from Fifa presidency but believes governing body can be reformedAs the rain whips around Oslo’s government quarter, Lise Klaveness is shielding herself from the wind, trying to work out tactics. “Of course we cannot probably do everything alone, but we have a voice, we have the right to speak, we have the right to suggest, so let’s see,” she says. “We will at least try to be a spearhead.”The president of the Norwegian Football Federation wants to re-engage Fifa, and other governing bodies, on the topic of remedy.

A slightly arcane aspect of human rights policy in normal times, the importance of remedy became very clear in the aftermath of the World Cup in Qatar, when the families of those injured or killed in the work that led up to the tournament were left without financial compensation after Fifa chose to direct a legacy fund elsewhere.
